meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

выручить.gloss: to help out, rescue, bail out

meanings.en: to help out, rescue, come to aid of
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ручить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to help out'.

examples.trans: A friend will always help out in trouble.

examples.text: Спасибо, друг, ты меня очень выручишь!
examples.trans: Thank you, friend, you will really help me out!
You saved me. That was quick thinking.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Давай работай быстрее, гости уже давно ждут заказ!
examples.trans: Come on, work faster, the guests have been waiting for their order for a long time!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оображать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'understand, use one’s head'.

examples.trans: You saved me. That was quick thinking.

examples.text: Ты меня просто выручила, очень быстро соображаешь в трудной ситуации!
examples.trans: You really saved me, you think very fast in a tough situation!

examples.text: К концу длинной смены я уже совсем плохо соображаю.
examples.trans: By the end of a long shift I am already thinking very poorly.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Conversational Russian particle ('all right') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'fine'.
меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.en: debtor, someone who owes money or books
meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'debtor', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.trans: Because you are a chronic debtor.
The bank phoned all the debtors.

examples.text: Я вообще вам могу ничего не давать! Потому что вы злостный должник.
examples.trans: I don't have to give you anything at all! Because you are a chronic debtor.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'всегда').

examples.trans: Say that you are leaving for good.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Secondary conversational sense ('owe') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'слуга'). Common feminine noun meaning 'service, favor' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I don't forget favors like that.

examples.text: Я такие важные услуги никогда не забываю.
examples.trans: I never forget such important services.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.en: by the way, speaking of which
meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'by the way'.
Secondary conversational sense ('handy, well-timed') (это очень кстати) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, by the way, I almost forgot.

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('that') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'
Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'girl'.

examples.text: Девушки, как я, у тебя не будет!
examples.trans: You'll never have a girl like me!

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'давать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'pass on, send'.

examples.text: А, кстати, та девушка ничего мне не передавала?
examples.trans: By the way, did that girl leave a message for me?

examples.text: Кстати, та девушка ничего для меня не передавала?
examples.trans: By the way, did that girl leave any message for me?

examples.text: Гости за пятым столиком передают огромную благодарность шефу.
examples.trans: The guests at table five send their huge thanks to the chef.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нятие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'concept, idea, notion' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.
Max, I have no idea at all.

meanings.note: mostly in set phrases: иметь совесть, иметь право = to have the right; everyday 'I have' is у меня есть

examples.trans: You have the right to remain silent.

examples.text: Нина, имей совесть! Я вчера ради вас всё сделал.
examples.trans: Nina, have a heart! Yesterday I did everything for you.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('even') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to see', forming an aspectual pair with 'увидеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = see?') (drawing attention) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.text: Ты видишь, сколько гостей сегодня вечером сидит в зале?
examples.trans: Do you see how many guests are sitting in the hall tonight?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'валить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'take off, dump'.

examples.text: Понятия не имею. Я даже не видела, как она свалила.
examples.trans: No idea. I did not even see her leave.

examples.text: Я даже не заметила, в какой момент она тихо свалила домой.
examples.trans: I did not even notice at what moment she quietly took off for home.

examples.text: Не пытайся свалить свою собственную ошибку на молодого стажёра.
examples.trans: Do not try to dump your own mistake onto the young intern.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'идти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'next'.
Secondary conversational sense ('next, go on') (in a list or a story) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: А дальше? Я очень волнуюсь, я к этому не приспособлена.
examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to forgive', forming an aspectual pair with 'прощать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('excuse me, sorry') (imperative: прости / простите) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask (for), to request', paired with 'просить'.

examples.trans: I wanted to ask you something.
Arkash, I wanted to ask you something.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'bill', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Или счёт в банке. Потому что они все обманщики.
examples.trans: Or a bank account. Because they are all cheats.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Secondary conversational sense ('still, yet') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('even (with comparatives)') (ещё больше = even more) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

посидеть.gloss: to sit for a while; to stay (with someone)

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'сидеть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to sit for a while', forming an aspectual pair with 'сидеть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to stay with, keep company') (посиди с ним = stay with him) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Stay with Vika for a while.
Let's sit in a café for a bit.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: Anikeev came here in person, and what?

examples.text: Пятнадцать лет мы просим новое здание! Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: For fifteen years we've been asking for a new building! Anikeev came here in person, and what?

meanings.note: кого-то за что-то = someone for something

examples.text: Но я просто не знаю, как вас поблагодарить.
examples.trans: But I just don't know how to thank you.
She thanked him for his help.
I would like to thank the chef personally.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'clear'.
Secondary conversational sense ('I see') (as a reply) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm going to be mayor, understood?
